nodes.name: SrIrO₃ sol-gel synthesis
nodes.procedure: 760 mg H₂IrCl₆·xH₂O and 1120 mg Sr(NO₃)₂ were added in the mixture of 16 mL ethylene glycol and 20 mL deionized H₂O. 1120 mg citric acid as the complexing agent was introduced into such solution. The pH value was regulated at about 10 by the introduction of the appropriate amount of KOH solution. After intensively stirring, the resulting uniform solution was heat-treated at 150°C for 12 h in an oven, gaining a dark xerogel precursor. Such precursor was sintered in air at 700°C for 6 h and was then treated into 1M HCl solution to receive the targeted monoclinic SrIrO₃ nanosheets.

nodes.source_text: Synthesis of SrIrO₃. Traditional sol-gel approach was adopted to prepare monoclinic SrIrO₃.[25] 760 mg H₂IrCl₆·xH₂O and 1120 mg Sr(NO₃)₂ were added... to receive the targeted monoclinic SrIrO₃ nanosheets.

nodes.name: CeO₂ quantum dots decoration
nodes.procedure: 50 mg of as-prepared SrIrO₃ was uniformly dispersed in 5 mL DMF. Meanwhile, a certain amount of Ce(NO₃)₃·6H₂O was dissolved into another 5 mL DMF. Next, the Ce(NO₃)₃ solution was dropwise added into SrIrO₃ suspension, followed by rapid stirring for 1 h. Subsequently, this resulting mixture was put into a water bath at 90°C for 0.5 h. After cooling to room temperature, the precipitate was washed with ethanol for several times. Finally, the precipitate was sintered at 400°C for 2 h to receive CeO₂ quantum dots decorated SrIrO₃ nanosheets heterostructure. By controlling the amount of Ce(NO₃)₃, 2 w.t.%, 4 w.t.% and 8 w.t.% CeO₂ deposited on SrIrO₃ were obtained, denoted as 2CeO₂@SrIrO3, 4CeO₂@SrIrO3 and 8CeO₂@SrIrO3, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: SrIrO3 exhibits monoclinic perovskite structure matching JCPDS-72-0855 with face-shared [IrO6] octahedrons. CeO2 decorated samples show only SrIrO3 characteristic peaks due to low CeO2 loading and quantum dot morphology.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 3b shows the XRD patterns of SrIrO3, 2CeO2@SrIrO3, 4CeO2@SrIrO3, and 8CeO2@SrIrO3. It is clear that the pristine SrIrO3 exhibits a monoclinic perovskite structure (Fig. S5), agreeing well with the referenced JCPDS-72-0855.

nodes.characterization_summary: 4CeO2@SrIrO3 shows visible Ce signal with increased Ce3+ concentration indicating rich oxygen vacancies. Ir 4f binding energies shift negatively by ~0.25 eV indicating reduced Ir valence state. O 1s shows increased adsorbed oxygen concentration.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in XPS survey scan (Fig. 3c), a visible intensity of Ce element is obtained on 4CeO2@SrIrO3 electrocatalyst... the binding energies of Ir 4f7/2 and Ir 4f5/2 peaks have the negative shift of ∼0.25 eV after CeO2 decoration.

nodes.characterization_summary: EPR signals at g=2.002 confirm oxygen vacancies with higher signal intensity for 4CeO2@SrIrO3 than pristine SrIrO3.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As presented in Fig. 3g, the EPR signals of g = 2.002 are well indexed to oxygen vacancies. The signal intensity of 4CeO2@SrIrO3 electrocatalyst is larger than that of SrIrO3 electrocatalyst.

nodes.characterization_summary: SrIrO3 adopts 2D nanosheets architecture ensuring rich exposed active sites. CeO2 quantum dots well-dispersed on 2CeO2@SrIrO3 and 4CeO2@SrIrO3 but show particle aggregation on 8CeO2@SrIrO3 at high loading.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in SEM images (Fig. S6), the individual SrIrO3 electrocatalyst adopts the 2D nanosheets architecture, which ensures rich exposed active sites and fast mass transportation... lots of CeO2 particles are obtained on 8CeO2@SrIrO3 surface because of the particle aggregation at high mass loading.

properties.description: Irregular sheet-like morphology with layered structures and rough surfaces

nodes.characterization_summary: SrIrO3 nanosheets expose (001) plane confirmed by lattice fringes of 0.282 nm (130) and 0.280 nm (200). 4CeO2@SrIrO3 shows uniform ~4 nm CeO2 quantum dots with 0.318 nm (111) spacing. FFT pattern and elemental mapping confirm 0D/2D heterostructure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the TEM image of Fig. 4b, the lattice fringes with interplanar spacings of 0.282 nm and 0.280 nm are, respectively, assigned to the (130) and (200) crystallographic planes of SrIrO3... lots of tiny CeO2 quantum dots (∼4 nm) are uniformly deposited onto the surface of SrIrO3 nanosheets (Fig. 4d).

nodes.characterization_summary: N2 adsorption-desorption isotherms used to determine specific surface areas of commercial IrO2, SrIrO3, 2CeO2@SrIrO3, 4CeO2@SrIrO3 and 8CeO2@SrIrO3 electrocatalysts.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Specific surface areas of electrocatalysts were evaluated by N2 adsorption-desorption isotherm approach... Fig. S7 presents the specific surface areas of commercial IrO2, SrIrO3, 2CeO2@SrIrO3, 4CeO2@SrIrO3 and 8CeO2@SrIrO3 electrocatalysts.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM confirms CeO2 (111) plane spacing of 0.318 nm on 4CeO2@SrIrO3 and SrIrO3 (130)/(200) planes. Post-OER HRTEM shows maintained lattice fringes for both phases with amorphous surface layer on uncoated SrIrO3 but stable CeO2 coating.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The obtained interplanar spacing of 0.318 nm is consistent with the (111) plane of CeO2 (Fig. 4e)... The lattice fringes with specific interplanar spacings are well assigned to both SrIrO3 and CeO2 phases, as illustrated in HRTEM image (Fig. 6e).
